steps.title: Import Angular core modules
steps.instruction: Add import statements for Component and OnInit from @angular/core.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbols you want to import, then specify the module path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing from @angular/core
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode: // Add import statements for Component and OnInit from @angular/core here
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the necessary imports to create an Angular component.
successCriteria: The import statement includes both Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Component and OnInit from @angular/core. These are essential for creating Angular components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import Component and OnInit from the @angular/core module.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class with @Component decorator and basic metadata. Add the class definition below the imports.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator with a selector and template. The class should implement OnInit.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';

// Create AppComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with @Component decorator and implements OnInit.
successCriteria: The code includes a class named AppComponent decorated with @Component, with selector and template properties, and implements OnInit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main AppComponent with the @Component decorator and basic metadata.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your AppComponent class has the @Component decorator with selector and template properties, and implements OnInit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent class definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use @Component decorator with selector and template, and implement OnInit.

steps.title: Add component template
steps.instruction: Add a template property to the @Component decorator with a basic HTML structure containing a heading and a paragraph.
steps.hint:
Inside the @Component decorator, add template: `'

Push Notifications

Welcome to push notifications!

'`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a basic HTML template that will render a heading and paragraph when the app runs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a template to your component. The template property defines the HTML structure that Angular will render for this component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the template property with valid HTML content containing both a heading and a paragraph.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have a proper template yet. Add a template property to the @Component decorator with basic HTML structure.

steps.title: Create notification service
steps.instruction: Generate a new service file named notification.service.ts and define a NotificationService class with the @Injectable decorator.
steps.hint: Use the Angular CLI command 'ng generate service notification' or manually create the file with the proper Angular service structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new service file (notification.service.ts) is created with a NotificationService class that can be injected into components.
successCriteria: The service file must contain a class named NotificationService decorated with @Injectable and exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the NotificationService. This service will handle all push notification logic separately from your components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a separate notification.service.ts file with a class named NotificationService that has the @Injectable decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service wasn't created correctly. You need to generate a new service file with the NotificationService class using Angular's service structure.

steps.title: Import service into component
steps.instruction: Inject the NotificationService into the AppComponent by adding it to the constructor parameters with proper dependency injection syntax.
steps.hint: Add a constructor parameter with the NotificationService type and the appropriate Angular decorator.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of injecting a service into a component
constructor(private dataService: DataService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationService will be available for use within the AppComponent through dependency injection.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully injected the NotificationService into your component. Now you can use its methods to implement push notifications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct dependency injection syntax with the private keyword and proper type annotation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationService injection isn't quite right. Remember to add it as a constructor parameter with the proper TypeScript type and Angular dependency injection syntax.

steps.title: Add notification state
steps.instruction: Add a notifications array property to the AppComponent class to store notification data.
steps.hint: Define a property in the class with type Notification[] (or any[]) and initialize it as an empty array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class now has a notifications property that can store an array of notification objects.
successCriteria: The component class should have a notifications property defined with array type annotation and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a notifications array property to the component. This will be used to store notification data that we'll display in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the notifications property is properly typed as an array and initialized as an empty array. Check that it's defined directly in the AppComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications array property is missing or incorrectly defined. In TypeScript/Angular, you need to add a property like 'notifications: any[] = [];' inside the AppComponent class.

steps.title: Define requestPermission method
steps.instruction: In the NotificationService class, add a method named requestPermission that returns a Promise<NotificationPermission>. Inside this method, call Notification.requestPermission() and return its result.
steps.hint: Use the Notification API's requestPermission method. Remember to return the promise.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationService now has a requestPermission method that can be called to request notification permissions from the user.
successCriteria: The NotificationService should have a method named requestPermission that returns a Promise<NotificationPermission> and calls Notification.requestPermission().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the requestPermission method to the NotificationService. This method will be used to request permission from the user to show notifications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the method might be missing the return type or the actual call to Notification.requestPermission(). Make sure the method returns a Promise<NotificationPermission> and calls Notification.requestPermission().
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationService doesn't have a properly defined requestPermission method. It should be a method that returns a Promise<NotificationPermission> and calls Notification.requestPermission().

steps.title: Define sendNotification method
steps.instruction: Add a sendNotification method to the NotificationService that creates a new notification using the Notification API.
steps.hint: Inside the NotificationService class, define a method called sendNotification that takes parameters like title and options, then calls new Notification() with them.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationService will have a sendNotification method that can create browser notifications.
successCriteria: The NotificationService class contains a sendNotification method with proper TypeScript parameter types that creates a new Notification instance.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the sendNotification method to your service. This method will be used to trigger browser notifications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check that it's named 'sendNotification', accepts parameters (title and options), and creates a new Notification instance.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationService doesn't yet have a properly defined sendNotification method. Make sure to add the method inside the class with the correct signature.

steps.title: Add permission button to template
steps.instruction: In the component template, add a button that calls the requestPermission method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="methodName()" to call the method on button click.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of adding a button that calls a method -->
<button (click)="requestPermission()">Request Permission</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Request Permission' appears in the template that will trigger the requestPermission method when clicked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that will request notification permission when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button has the correct event binding to call the requestPermission method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly configured. Check that you're using Angular's (click) event binding syntax.

steps.title: Add notification button to template
steps.instruction: Add a button to the template that calls the sendNotification method on click. Place it after the existing permission button comment.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="sendNotification()" to call the method when the button is clicked.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of adding a button with click handler -->
<button (click)="sendNotification()">Send Test Notification</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a button that will trigger the sendNotification method when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element should be present in the template with (click)="sendNotification()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button to send test notifications. The button is properly wired to call the sendNotification method when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it might be missing the click event binding or the method call. Make sure to use (click)="sendNotification()" to properly connect the button to the method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button with the click handler wasn't found. You need to add a button element with (click)="sendNotification()" in the template.

steps.title: Display notifications list
steps.instruction: Add an *ngFor directive to the template to display the notifications array from the NotificationService. Create a list item for each notification.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor to iterate over notificationService.notifications and display each notification's title and body.
steps.analogousExample: • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template should include an unordered list that displays each notification's title and body using *ngFor.
successCriteria: The code should include *ngFor directive iterating over notificationService.notifications and display notification properties in list items.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the *ngFor directive to display the notifications list. The template now shows each notification's title and body.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using *ngFor correctly and accessing the notifications array from the notificationService.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the notifications list. Remember to use *ngFor to iterate over notificationService.notifications and show each notification's details.

steps.title: Update notifications on send
steps.instruction: Modify the sendNotification method in your NotificationComponent to add a new notification object to the notifications array when called.
steps.hint: Inside the sendNotification method, push a new object with a title and timestamp into the notifications array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The sendNotification method will now update the notifications array with a new notification object each time it's called.
successCriteria: The sendNotification method should push a new object into the notifications array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully updated the sendNotification method to add new notifications to the array. This completes the basic push notification implementation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're pushing a complete notification object with both title and timestamp properties into the notifications array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sendNotification method should add a new notification object to the notifications array. Try using the push method on the notifications array.
